summary:
Iyök is a bilingual (English/Spanish) web tool for investigating Earth system trends with NASA data, built by Bee4TheWorld. Our MVP focuses on mainland Costa Rica. It turns NASA's IMERG Final V07 monthly precipitation (2001–2024, 288 months) into a reproducible area-weighted series, clipped to the official IGN (Instituto Geográfico Nacional, Costa Rica) boundary. Users can explore it through a synchronized chart, a grid-cell map and a world map.
For the challenge, Iyök tackles what changes, where and by how much, and keeps evidence in view. Each result shows its product, version, unit conversion, weighting method, monthly coverage and limitations. A trend is reported as inconclusive until the method and its assumptions pass scientific review. We never claim significance or causation the data cannot support.
This matters because Central America's rainfall drives water, agriculture and disaster risk. Transparent, verifiable analysis helps communities, students and decision-makers tell real change from noise.
details:
Iyök is a bilingual (English/Spanish) web platform for investigating Earth system trends with NASA data. Our MVP studies monthly precipitation over mainland Costa Rica from 2001 to 2024. A Python backend gets NASA's IMERG Final V07 monthly product through NASA Harmony and clips it to the official IGN (Instituto Geográfico Nacional, Costa Rica) boundary. It then computes an area-weighted monthly series. Users explore it through a chart, a synchronized grid-cell map, a data table, a completeness panel and a full provenance sheet. Trends are estimated with Sen's slope and an autocorrelation-corrected Mann-Kendall test. They are reported as inconclusive until the method passes scientific review.

Rainfall drives water, agriculture, energy and disaster risk in Central America. Iyök makes satellite evidence understandable for students, communities and decision-makers without hiding its limits. The method can later be extended to other Latin American regions, validating each one separately.

Next.js, React, TypeScript, MapLibre GL and ECharts on the frontend. Python, FastAPI, xarray, NumPy, SciPy and Shapely on the backend. NASA Earthdata (Harmony, GES DISC), Vercel, Supabase, and Playwright and pytest for testing. We used AI coding assistants during development, but no AI generates or interprets the data shown.

Evidence is part of the interface: every result shows its product version, method, coverage and limitations. Maps use the same data and boundary as the calculation. We separate observation from inference, note IMERG's biases in mountains and along coasts, check licenses, design for accessibility and mobile, and never claim NASA endorsement.
